title: Enrolled, billed, gone: payments set against the enrollment record
question: Was a provider paid before any enrollment record begins, did a new enrollee reach the top of the national table within a year, and did anyone leave soon after a peak?
finding: Of 766 San Francisco billing numbers with payments, 29 were paid $10.7 million for months that no enrollment record under that number covers; 4 of the 115 whose first record begins in 2018 or later were among the top 10 in 100 billers nationwide for a service within twelve months (2 in the top 1 in 100); 35 numbers paid $3.5 million have no enrollment record at all; and 93 numbers paid $8.6 million are recorded in California only as “active, do not pay”. The third question cannot be answered from this file: none of the 665 San Francisco billing numbers with a California record has an end date, so a provider that left after a peak cannot be seen.
how: The federal enrollment file lists periods of Medicaid enrollment by State, each with a start date, an end date, a status and a provider type. For each San Francisco billing number, every month with a payment was checked against every period under that number in any State (an open-ended period covers everything after its start). A new enrollee is a number whose earliest period begins in 2018 or later; its payments for each service in the twelve months from its first paid month or its start date, whichever is earlier, were set against the amount that puts a biller in the national top 10 in 100 and top 1 in 100 for that service in a calendar year (the higher of the two years the window touches; services with 50 or more billers). Rows need $25,000 outside a period, $100,000 with no record, or, for organizations only, $250,000 under a do-not-pay status; individual practitioners under that status are counted and not listed.
limits: What the file can show is thin for California. Of 2,099,914 California records, 50% carry no provider number at all, 70% have a placeholder start date in 1900 or 1970, only 28,660 have an end date, and the only statuses are “active - active” and “active - active do not pay”: no California record says a provider was terminated. The federal documentation says the file keeps one provider number for each State enrollment record, so an organization enrolled under a different number, or under a record with no number, looks unenrolled here; it also says the State is the authority on enrollment.  The documentation does not define “active, do not pay”; it may describe providers enrolled only to order or refer, or paid through a group. Other States’ records do carry termination codes against 66 San Francisco billing numbers, 13 of them numbers of the City or the University of California; 13 of those 13 were still being paid in 2024, so a code in another State’s records cannot be read as a finding about a provider and may only mean it stopped billing that State; none of the 66 numbers is on the federal exclusion list, and the codes are not used here. 2024 is preliminary and small cells are withheld.
